rationale: Reading the recovery entry while working the accept-status premise produced a separate, sharper lead that belongs to its own question: startRecoveryForInstance raises the recovering replica's own vbal to the newly made ballot before building the self PrepareReply, so the self entry reports the new ballot as its VBallot while lb.ballot was seeded with the old vbal. Inside handlePrepareReply the selection rule is element.VBallot >= lb.ballot with lb.ballot updated as the loop runs, so the self entry raises the running ballot to the new one and every remote reply whose vbal is below the new ballot is then skipped. This product opens that as the next Candidate, keeps the accept-status Candidate open, and records no map change so the map basis stays stable.

question.question: startRecoveryForInstance seeds LeaderBookkeeping with lb.ballot = the record's old vbal, then makes a new ballot and sets inst.bal and inst.vbal to that new ballot before constructing its own PrepareReply, so the self entry's VBallot is the new ballot. handlePrepareReply keeps the attributes of every reply with element.VBallot >= lb.ballot while lb.ballot is raised to each accepted VBallot. Does that ordering make the recovering replica's own entry raise the running ballot past every remote reply that holds the committed or accepted value at an older vbal, so that the selection ignores a committed value announced by another replica and the resolution proceeds from the local record (sub-case 6 restart, NOOP when no local command is known) instead of re-proposing the committed vector?
question.importance: If the recovering replica can ignore a remote reply that reports COMMITTED with a committed (Seq, Deps, Command) vector, recovery would re-propose a different value for an instance that some replica has already committed and may already have executed; replicas that installed the commit return early on a later Commit, so the two vectors would coexist and the state machines could diverge. That is an agreement and state-convergence consequence, not a performance one. The same rule decides whether an accepted value is re-proposed or replaced by a phase-1 restart.

counterevidence: scoped to the seed: lb.ballot is assigned the record's old vbal before the new ballot is made, so the running maximum starts below the self entry's VBallot, which is what lets the self entry raise it (S14-recovery-start-prepare)

scoped to remote replies: a remote replica raises only its bal in handlePrepare and reports its stored vbal, so a reply that holds a value accepted at an older ballot reports a VBallot below the new ballot and is skipped by the comparison (S14-recovery-start-prepare)

scoped to the launched configuration: makeBallot starts from the local id (plus N when the replica is not the instance owner) and only raises while IsLeader is set, so the new ballot can also be lower than a remote vbal that was raised by an earlier recovery, which would invert the skipping (S5-broadcasters, S24-runReplica-epaxos)

scoped to the commit branch: the committed vector is reported as PrepareReply.Command, and the selection loop assigns lb.cmds from the element that passes the vbal test, so the committed command is only adopted when that element passes (S15-handlePrepareReply, S13-handleCommit)

question.trigger_rationale: This is an A2 relationship question: which value a leadership transfer may adopt is decided by the ballot context each reply carries (Bal for the promise, VBal for the value that could have been committed), and the recovering replica is the one that reports both for its own record. The discrepancy is inside the recovery entry itself and is visible in the field values being built: lb.ballot is seeded from the old vbal, then inst.vbal is overwritten with the new ballot and immediately copied into the self PrepareReply's VBallot. Because handlePrepareReply treats element.VBallot >= lb.ballot as the condition for adopting a reply's attributes and mutates lb.ballot as it goes, the self entry's value determines whether remote replies at older vbals are considered at all. The discriminator is therefore a question of ordering and comparison, which a source review plus a controlled schedule (a recovering replica plus one committed and one accepted reply) can settle.

feedback.answered: The accept-status Candidate's counterevidence is now sharper: the leader-side accept branch records ACCEPTED together with the merged attributes, so recovery sub-case 2 can be reached through a recovering replica's own record, while an accept-only acceptor reports accepted attributes with Status NONE and no command. While tracing that, the recovery entry's own vbal handling surfaced as a separate mechanism: the recovering replica reports the newly made ballot as its VBallot, which under the element.VBallot >= lb.ballot comparison can place the running maximum above every remote value at an older vbal.
remaining: whether the recovery value selection can ignore a remote COMMITTED reply and therefore re-propose a different vector for an instance already committed elsewhere (S14-recovery-start-prepare, S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether an accept-only acceptor's command-less reply at the accepted vbal can be preferred over an equal-vbal reply that carries the pre-accepted value, and whether that shifts the resolution to a phase-1 restart (S11-handleAccept, S15-handlePrepareReply)
whether a controlled schedule with one committed reply and one accepted reply can settle both questions without altering protocol code (S15-handlePrepareReply)
feedback.rationale: The new Candidate is kept to the recovery value selection because that is where a decision can change as a result of the vbal the recovering replica reports; the accept-status question stays open with its own proposition and is not folded in. No map object is changed, so the existing B9/B11 unknowns continue to describe the same recovery responsibilities at the level already recorded.
